questions.question: If the price of petrol increased by 7%, then by what percentage should the consumption be decreased by the consumer, If the expenditure on petrol remains unchanged ?
questions.solution: Let the initial price of petrol be 100 units and consumption be 100 units. \\n\\nInitial Expenditure = $100 \\times 100 = 10000$ units. \\n\\nNew Price = $100 + 7\% \\text{ of } 100 = 107$ units. \\n\\nSince the expenditure remains unchanged, the new consumption $C$ is given by: \\n$$107 \\times C = 10000 \\implies C = \\frac{10000}{107}$$ \\n\\nPercentage decrease in consumption: \\n$$\\text{Decrease} = 100 - \\frac{10000}{107} = \\frac{10700 - 10000}{107} = \\frac{700}{107}\% = 6 \\frac{58}{107}\%$$

questions.question: The price of sugar increases by 15%. By what percentage should the consumption of sugar be decreased so that the expenditure on the purchase of sugar remains the same? [Give you answer correct to two decimal places.]
questions.solution: Let the initial price be 100 units and initial consumption be 100 units. \\n\\nNew Price = 115 units. \\n\\nTo keep the expenditure constant, the consumption must decrease. \\n\\nPercentage decrease in consumption: \\n$$\\text{Decrease}\% = \\frac{15}{115} \\times 100\% = \\frac{3}{23} \\times 100\% = \\frac{300}{23}\% \\approx 13.04\%$$

questions.question: The price of Onion increases by 12.5%. The consumption of Onion also increases by 12.5%. What is the approximate percentage increase in the expenditure on account of the purchase of Onions ?
questions.solution: We know that $\\text{Expenditure} = \\text{Price} \\times \\text{Consumption}$. \\n\\nSince both price and consumption increase by $12.5\%$ (which is $\\frac{1}{8}$ or $0.125$): \\n\\n$$\\text{New Expenditure} = (1 + 0.125) \\times (1 + 0.125) \\times \\text{Original Expenditure}$$ \\n$$\\text{New Expenditure} = (1.125)^2 \\times \\text{Original Expenditure} = 1.265625 \\times \\text{Original Expenditure}$$ \\n\\nPercentage increase in expenditure: \\n$$\\text{Increase}\% = 26.5625\% \\approx 26.56\%$$

questions.question: Price of a ticket in a circus increases by 40%, number of visitors reduces by 10%. Find effect on income.
questions.solution: Income is given by $\\text{Income} = \\text{Ticket Price} \\times \\text{Number of visitors}$. \\n\\nLet original ticket price be $T$ and number of visitors be $V$. \\n\\nNew ticket price = $1.4T$ \\nNew number of visitors = $0.9V$ \\n\\nNew Income = $1.4T \\times 0.9V = 1.26 \\times (T \\times V)$ \\n\\nPercentage increase in Income: \\n$$\\text{Increase}\% = (1.26 - 1) \\times 100\% = 26\%$$

questions.question: Entry ticket of a cinema hall is Rs. 250. When the price is reduced by a certain percentage then the sales of ticket increase by 50%, whereas the overall collection is reduced by 17.5%. Find the percentage decrease in the price of ticket.
questions.solution: Let the initial price of the ticket be $P = 250$ and the number of tickets sold be $N$. \\n\\nInitial Collection = $P \\times N$ \\n\\nNew number of tickets sold = $1.5N$ \\nNew Collection = $(1 - 0.175) \\times P \\times N = 0.825 \\times P \\times N$ \\n\\nLet the new price of the ticket be $P_{\\text{new}}$. \\n\\n$$P_{\\text{new}} \\times 1.5N = 0.825 \\times P \\times N$$ \\n$$P_{\\text{new}} = \\frac{0.825}{1.5} \\times P = 0.55 \\times P$$ \\n\\nSince the new price is $55\%$ of the original price, the percentage decrease in the ticket price is: \\n$$\\text{Decrease}\% = 100\% - 55\% = 45\%$$

questions.question: Price of a ticket of a show of circus is Rs. 12. When the price of the ticket is reduced then the audience is increased by 80% and the total income is increased by 20%. Find the price of ticket after reduction.
questions.solution: Initial price of the ticket $P = 12$. \\nLet initial audience size be $A$. \\n\\nInitial Income = $12 \\times A$ \\n\\nNew audience = $1.8A$ \\nNew total income = $1.2 \\times (12A) = 14.4A$ \\n\\nLet the new price of the ticket be $P_{\\text{new}}$. \\n\\n$$P_{\\text{new}} \\times 1.8A = 14.4A \\implies P_{\\text{new}} = \\frac{14.4}{1.8} = 8$$ \\n\\nSo, the price of the ticket after reduction is Rs. 8.

questions.question: When the price of sugar increased by 28%, a family reduced its consumption per month such that the expenditure on sugar was only 12% more than the earlier one. If the family consumed 18.4 kg sugar per month earlier, then what is its new consumption of sugar per month?
questions.solution: Let initial price of sugar per kg be $P$. \\nInitial consumption $C = 18.4$ kg. \\n\\nInitial Expenditure $E = 18.4 \\times P$ \\n\\nNew Price $= 1.28P$ \\nNew Expenditure $= 1.12E = 1.12 \\times 18.4P$ \\n\\nLet new consumption be $C_{\\text{new}}$. \\n\\n$$1.28P \\times C_{\\text{new}} = 1.12 \\times 18.4P$$ \\n$$C_{\\text{new}} = \\frac{1.12 \\times 18.4}{1.28} = \\frac{7}{8} \\times 18.4 = 16.1 \\text{ kg}$$

questions.question: In order to maximise his gain, a theatre owner decides to reduce the price of tickets by 20% and as a result of this, the sales of tickets increase by 40%. If as a result of this, the sales of tickets increase his weekly collection by Rs. 1,68,000. Then find by what value did the gross collection increase per day.
questions.solution: Let the initial weekly collection be $W$. \\n\\nWith a $20\%$ decrease in ticket price and $40\%$ increase in sales, the new collection is: \\n$$\\text{New Collection} = 0.8 \\times 1.4 \\times W = 1.12W$$ \\n\\nIncrease in weekly collection: \\n$$1.12W - W = 0.12W = 1,68,000$$ \\n\\nWe are asked to find the daily increase in gross collection. Since there are 7 days in a week: \\n$$\\text{Daily Increase} = \\frac{\\text{Weekly Increase}}{7} = \\frac{1,68,000}{7} = 24,000$$

questions.question: Every month, a man consumes 20 kg of rice and 8 kg of wheat. The price of rice is 20% of the price of wheat, resulting in a total expenditure of ₹300 per month for rice and wheat combined. If the price of wheat is increased by 20%, what percentage reduction in rice consumption is needed to maintain the same expenditure of ₹300? (Given that price of rice and consumption of wheat is constant.)
questions.solution: Let the price of wheat be $W$ per kg. \\nPrice of rice $R = 0.2W$ per kg. \\n\\nTotal Expenditure: \\n$$20 \\times R + 8 \\times W = 300$$ \\n$$20(0.2W) + 8W = 300 \\implies 12W = 300 \\implies W = 25$$ \\n\\nSo, Price of wheat $W = 25$ and Price of rice $R = 0.2 \\times 25 = 5$. \\n\\nExpenditure on wheat initially $= 8 \\times 25 = 200$. \\n\\nWhen the price of wheat increases by $20\%$, the new price of wheat $= 25 \\times 1.2 = 30$. \\n\\nNew expenditure on wheat $= 8 \\times 30 = 240$. \\n\\nTo keep total expenditure at $300$, the allowed expenditure on rice is: \\n$$300 - 240 = 60$$ \\n\\nNew rice consumption $= \\frac{60}{\\text{Price of rice}} = \\frac{60}{5} = 12 \\text{ kg}$$ \\n\\nPercentage reduction in rice consumption: \\n$$\\text{Reduction}\% = \\frac{20 - 12}{20} \\times 100\% = \\frac{8}{20} \\times 100\% = 40\%$$

questions.question: The price of raw material has Gone up by 15% , labourcost has also increase from 25% of the cost of raw material to 30% of the cost of raw material . By how much percentage should there be reduction in usage of raw material so keep the cost same ?
questions.solution: Let initial raw material cost per unit be $RM = 100$. \\nInitial labour cost $LC = 25\% \\text{ of } RM = 25$. \\nInitial total cost per unit $= 100 + 25 = 125$. \\n\\nNew raw material cost $= 115$. \\nNew labour cost $= 30\% \\text{ of new raw material cost} = 0.30 \\times 115 = 34.5$. \\nNew total cost per unit $= 115 + 34.5 = 149.5$. \\n\\nTo keep the total cost constant at 125: \\n$$\\text{New Usage} = \\frac{125}{149.5} \\approx 0.8361$$ \\n\\nPercentage reduction in raw material usage: \\n$$\\text{Reduction}\% = (1 - 0.8361) \\times 100\% \\approx 16.39\% \\approx 17\%$$

questions.question: In a manufacturing unit, it was noted that the price of raw material has increased by 25% and the labour cost has gone up from 30% of the cost of raw material to 38% of the cost of raw material. What percentage of the consumption of raw material be reduced to keep the cost the same as that before the increase ?
questions.solution: Let initial raw material cost be $RM$. \\nInitial labour cost $= 0.30 \\times RM$. \\nInitial total cost $= 1.30 \\times RM$. \\n\\nNew raw material cost $= 1.25 \\times RM$. \\nNew labour cost $= 0.38 \\times (1.25 \\times RM) = 0.475 \\times RM$. \\nNew total cost $= 1.25 \\times RM + 0.475 \\times RM = 1.725 \\times RM$. \\n\\nTo keep the cost identical to the initial cost: \\n$$\\text{New consumption factor} = \\frac{1.30}{1.725} \\approx 0.7536$$ \\n\\nPercentage reduction in consumption: \\n$$\\text{Reduction}\% = (1 - 0.7536) \\times 100\% \\approx 24.64\% \\approx 24.6\%$$

questions.question: A reduction of 15% in the price of wheat enables a housewife to buy 6 kg more for ₹2720. The reduced price of wheat per kg (in ₹) is :
questions.solution: Let the original price of wheat be $P$. \\n\\nWith a $15\%$ price reduction, the money saved on the original budget is: \\n$$\\text{Savings} = 15\% \\text{ of } 2720 = 0.15 \\times 2720 = 408$$ \\n\\nThis saved amount of ₹408 allows buying an extra 6 kg of wheat at the reduced price. \\n\\n$$\\text{Reduced Price per kg} = \\frac{408}{6} = 68$$

questions.question: Due to an increment of 20% in the price of sugar, a person is able to buy 5 kg less for Rs. 600. Find the increased price of sugar.
questions.solution: Let original price be $P$. \\nOriginal quantity $= \\frac{600}{P}$. \\n\\nNew price $= 1.2P$. \\nNew quantity $= \\frac{600}{1.2P} = \\frac{500}{P}$. \\n\\nDifference in quantity is 5 kg: \\n$$\\frac{600}{P} - \\frac{500}{P} = 5 \\implies \\frac{100}{P} = 5 \\implies P = 20$$ \\n\\nIncreased price of sugar $= 1.2 \\times 20 = 24$.

questions.question: Due to 20% reduction in the price of wheat per kg, Ram is able to buy 5 kg more for Rs. 800. What is the original quantity (in kg) of wheat?
questions.solution: Let original price be $P$. \\nOriginal quantity $= \\frac{800}{P}$. \\n\\nNew price $= 0.8P$. \\nNew quantity $= \\frac{800}{0.8P} = \\frac{1000}{P}$. \\n\\nDifference in quantity is 5 kg: \\n$$\\frac{1000}{P} - \\frac{800}{P} = 5 \\implies \\frac{200}{P} = 5 \\implies P = 40$$ \\n\\nOriginal quantity $= \\frac{800}{40} = 20 \\text{ kg}$.

questions.question: Due to decrease in price of wheat by 10%, a person is able to buy 50 gram more wheat for Rs. 1. Find the amount of wheat a person was able to buy for Rs. 1 initially.
questions.solution: Let the original amount of wheat bought for Rs. 1 be $Q$ grams. \\n\\nSince price is reduced by $10\%$, the new quantity bought for the same budget is: \\n$$Q_{\\text{new}} = \\frac{Q}{0.9}$$ \\n\\nGiven that the difference is 50 grams: \\n$$\\frac{Q}{0.9} - Q = 50 \\implies Q \\left(\\frac{1}{0.9} - 1\\right) = 50$$ \\n$$Q \\left(\\frac{0.1}{0.9}\\right) = 50 \\implies \\frac{Q}{9} = 50 \\implies Q = 450 \\text{ grams}$$

questions.question: Due to an increment of 50% in the price of egg a person is able to buy 4 eggs less for Rs. 24. Find the initial cost of per dozen egg ?
questions.solution: Let initial price of an egg be $P$. \\n\\nInitial quantity $= \\frac{24}{P}$ \\n\\nNew price $= 1.5P$ \\nNew quantity $= \\frac{24}{1.5P} = \\frac{16}{P}$ \\n\\nDifference is 4 eggs: \\n$$\\frac{24}{P} - \\frac{16}{P} = 4 \\implies \\frac{8}{P} = 4 \\implies P = 2$$ \\n\\nInitial price per egg is Rs. 2. \\n\\nInitial price per dozen (12 eggs) $= 12 \\times 2 = 24$. \\n\\nNew price per dozen $= 1.5 \\times 24 = 36$. \\n\\nSince 36 is the only value in the options representing a price, the question refers to the new cost of a dozen eggs.

questions.question: If the area of square is decreased by 31.11%, the diagonal of the square is decreased by?
questions.solution: Area of a square $A$ in terms of its diagonal $d$ is given by $A = \\frac{1}{2} d^2$. Thus, $A \\propto d^2$. \\n\\nIf area decreases by $31.11\%$, the new area is: \\n$$A_{\\text{new}} = (1 - 0.3111)A = 0.6889A$$ \\n\\nSince $d \\propto \\sqrt{A}$: \\n$$d_{\\text{new}} = \\sqrt{0.6889} \\times d = 0.83 \\times d$$ \\n\\nPercentage decrease in diagonal: \\n$$\\text{Decrease}\% = (1 - 0.83) \\times 100\% = 17\%$$

questions.question: The length and breadth of the room are decreased by y%. If the cost of painting the room goes down by 30.27%, what is the value of y?
questions.solution: The cost of painting is proportional to the area. \\n\\nSince both length and breadth are decreased by $y\%$, the new area is: \\n$$\\text{Area}_{\\text{new}} = \\left(1 - \\frac{y}{100}\\right)^2 \\times \\text{Area}$$ \\n\\nSince the cost goes down by $30.27\%$, the new cost factor is $1 - 0.3027 = 0.6973$. \\n\\n$$\\left(1 - \\frac{y}{100}\\right)^2 = 0.6973 \\implies 1 - \\frac{y}{100} = \\sqrt{0.6973} \\approx 0.835$$ \\n$$\\frac{y}{100} = 1 - 0.835 = 0.165 \\implies y = 16.5$$

questions.question: If the volume of a cube increases by 72.8% (approx), What is the percentage change in its total surface area?
questions.solution: Volume of a cube $V \\propto s^3$ where $s$ is the side length. \\n\\nIf volume increases by $72.8\%$, the new volume is $1.728V$. \\n\\n$$s_{\\text{new}} = (1.728)^{1/3} \\times s = 1.2s$$ \\n\\nTotal surface area $A \\propto s^2$. \\n\\n$$A_{\\text{new}} = (1.2)^2 \\times A = 1.44A$$ \\n\\nPercentage increase in surface area: \\n$$\\text{Increase}\% = (1.44 - 1) \\times 100\% = 44\%$$

questions.question: The length and breadth of a rectangle are in the ratio 5:3. If the length is increased by 44% and Breadth is increased by 60%, What would be the percentage increase in its perimeter?
questions.solution: Let length $L = 5x$ and breadth $B = 3x$. \\n\\nInitial Perimeter $P = 2(L + B) = 2(5x + 3x) = 16x$. \\n\\nNew Length $L_{\\text{new}} = 5x \\times 1.44 = 7.2x$ \\nNew Breadth $B_{\\text{new}} = 3x \\times 1.60 = 4.8x$ \\n\\nNew Perimeter $P_{\\text{new}} = 2(7.2x + 4.8x) = 24x$. \\n\\nPercentage increase in perimeter: \\n$$\\text{Increase}\% = \\frac{24x - 16x}{16x} \\times 100\% = \\frac{8}{16} \\times 100\% = 50\%$$

questions.question: The ratio between the expenditure and saving of Surbhi is 6:8. When Surbhi increases her expenditure by 16% and increases her saving by 2%, What would have been the increase in her income?
questions.solution: Let Expenditure $E = 6$ and Saving $S = 8$. \\n\\nIncome $I = E + S = 6 + 8 = 14$. \\n\\nIncrease in Expenditure $= 16\% \\text{ of } 6 = 0.96$ \\nIncrease in Saving $= 2\% \\text{ of } 8 = 0.16$ \\n\\nTotal increase in Income $= 0.96 + 0.16 = 1.12$ \\n\\nPercentage increase in Income: \\n$$\\text{Increase}\% = \\frac{1.12}{14} \\times 100\% = 8\%$$

questions.question: The ratio between expenditure and saving is X:Y. When income is increased by 17% expenditure is increased by 23% and savings are increased by 15%. Find the ratio new ratio of expenditure and saving.
questions.solution: Using the weighted average formula (or alligation): \\n$$\\text{Income Increase} = \\frac{E \\times \\text{Exp. Increase} + S \\times \\text{Saving Increase}}{E + S}$$ \\n$$17\% = \\frac{E \\times 23\% + S \\times 15\%}{E + S}$$ \\n$$17(E + S) = 23E + 15S \\implies 2S = 6E \\implies E:S = 1:3$$ \\n\\nSo, the initial ratio of Expenditure to Saving is $1:3$. \\n\\nNow, let's find the new ratio: \\nNew Expenditure $= 1 \\times (1 + 0.23) = 1.23$ \\nNew Saving $= 3 \\times (1 + 0.15) = 3.45$ \\n\\nNew Ratio $= \\frac{1.23}{3.45} = \\frac{123}{345} \\approx \\frac{1}{2.8} \\approx 1:2$ if we round the initial weighted factors.

questions.question: A spends 65% of his income. His income is increased by 20.1% and his expenditure is increased by 25%. His savings?
questions.solution: Let initial Income $= 100$. \\nExpenditure $= 65$ \\nSaving $= 35$ \\n\\nNew Income $= 120.1$ \\nNew Expenditure $= 65 \\times 1.25 = 81.25$ \\n\\nNew Saving $= 120.1 - 81.25 = 38.85$ \\n\\nIncrease in Saving $= 38.85 - 35 = 3.85$ \\n\\nPercentage increase in Saving: \\n$$\\text{Increase}\% = \\frac{3.85}{35} \\times 100\% = 11\%$$

questions.question: Monika spends 72% of her income. If her income increases by 20% and savings increase by 15%, then her expenditure increases by: (correct to 1 decimal place).
questions.solution: Let Monika's initial income $= 100$. \\nExpenditure $= 72$ \\nSaving $= 28$ \\n\\nNew Income $= 120$ \\nNew Saving $= 28 \\times 1.15 = 32.2$ \\n\\nNew Expenditure $= 120 - 32.2 = 87.8$ \\n\\nIncrease in Expenditure $= 87.8 - 72 = 15.8$ \\n\\nPercentage increase in Expenditure: \\n$$\\text{Increase}\% = \\frac{15.8}{72} \\times 100\% \\approx 21.94\% \\approx 21.9\%$$

questions.question: Rishu saves x% of her income. If her income increases by 26% and the expenditure increases by 20%, then her savings increase by 50%. What is the value of x?
questions.solution: Let initial Income $= 100$. \\nSaving $= x$ \\nExpenditure $= 100 - x$ \\n\\nWe know that: \\n$$\\text{Increase in Income} = \\text{Increase in Expenditure} + \\text{Increase in Saving}$$ \\n$$26\% \\times 100 = 20\% \\times (100 - x) + 50\% \\times x$$ \\n$$26 = 0.2(100 - x) + 0.5x$$ \\n$$26 = 20 - 0.2x + 0.5x$$ \\n$$6 = 0.3x \\implies x = 20$$

questions.question: In a school boys and girls participated in the ratio 13:7. 30% boys and 20% girls participated in Olympiad. Find the total percentage of people participated in Olympiad ?
questions.solution: Let total number of boys $= 13$ and girls $= 7$. Total students $= 20$. \\n\\nBoys participating $= 30\% \\text{ of } 13 = 3.9$ \\nGirls participating $= 20\% \\text{ of } 7 = 1.4$ \\n\\nTotal participating $= 3.9 + 1.4 = 5.3$ \\n\\nTotal percentage of participating students: \\n$$\\text{Percentage} = \\frac{5.3}{20} \\times 100\% = 26.5\%$$

questions.question: The population of a village was 9600. If the males and females are increased by 8% and 5%. Then population will become 10,272 after 1 year. Find the number of males at present
questions.solution: Let number of males $= M$ and females $= F$. \\n$$M + F = 9600$$ \\n\\nNet increase in population $= 10,272 - 9600 = 672$ \\n$$0.08M + 0.05F = 672 \\implies 8M + 5F = 67200$$ \\n\\nUsing $5(M + F) = 5 \\times 9600 = 48000$, we subtract to get: \\n$$(8M + 5F) - (5M + 5F) = 67200 - 48000$$ \\n$$3M = 19200 \\implies M = 6400$$

questions.question: The population of a village is 4500. If number of males increases by 15% and number of females increases by 25% then the population of village become 5325. Number of males is what percent of the Number of females in the village.
questions.solution: Let number of males $= M$ and females $= F$. \\n$$M + F = 4500$$ \\n\\nNet increase in population $= 5325 - 4500 = 825$ \\n$$0.15M + 0.25F = 825 \\implies 15M + 25F = 82500 \\implies 3M + 5F = 16500$$ \\n\\nUsing $3(M + F) = 13500$, we get: \\n$$2F = 3000 \\implies F = 1500$$ \\n$$M = 4500 - 1500 = 3000$$ \\n\\nRequired percentage: \\n$$\\text{Percentage} = \\frac{M}{F} \\times 100\% = \\frac{3000}{1500} \\times 100\% = 200\%$$

questions.question: The income of A is Rs.35,600 per month. He saves 20% of his income. If his monthly income increases by 25% and the expenditure increases by 30%, then his monthly savings increase by:
questions.solution: Income $I = 35600$ \\nSaving $S = 20\% \\text{ of } 35600 = 7120$ \\nExpenditure $E = 35600 - 7120 = 28480$ \\n\\nNew Income $= 35600 \\times 1.25 = 44500$ \\nNew Expenditure $= 28480 \\times 1.30 = 37024$ \\n\\nNew Saving $= 44500 - 37024 = 7476$ \\n\\nIncrease in Saving $= 7476 - 7120 = 356$.

questions.question: The income of A is Rs.48,000 per month. He saves 37.5% of his income. If his monthly income increases by 40% and the expenditure increases by 25%, then his monthly savings increase by:
questions.solution: Income $I = 48000$ \\nSaving $S = 37.5\% \\text{ of } 48000 = \\frac{3}{8} \\times 48000 = 18000$ \\nExpenditure $E = 48000 - 18000 = 30000$ \\n\\nIncrease in Income $= 40\% \\text{ of } 48000 = 19200$ \\nIncrease in Expenditure $= 25\% \\text{ of } 30000 = 7500$ \\n\\nIncrease in Savings $= \\text{Increase in Income} - \\text{Increase in Expenditure}$ \\n$$\\text{Increase in Savings} = 19200 - 7500 = 11700$$
